source.title: An electrically coupled pioneer circuit enables motor development via proprioceptive feedback in Drosophila embryos.

confidence_rationale: Clean causal embryonic experiment with a genetic deprivation manipulation and circuit-level identification. It is mixed rather than supporting because it cuts both ways for CDQ-007: it is a demonstrator-free bootstrap (nothing outside the embryo teaches it), which favours H-approach-primitive; but it also shows the innate circuit is INSUFFICIENT alone and requires self-generated experience to mature, which weakens a naive 'just add an innate drive and competence follows' reading. Invertebrate embryo, so transfer_risk is non-trivial.
failure_signatures: The innate pioneer circuit does NOT produce a mature CPG on its own -- proprioceptive feedback from self-generated movement is REQUIRED. An innate primitive that is never exercised does not mature into competence.

The 'teacher' here is the agent's own body via proprioception, which has no obvious REE analog if the substrate lacks a reafference channel; a REE approach-primitive with no self-generated-experience loop would not reproduce this mechanism.
Drosophila embryonic motor development is several transfer steps from vertebrate goal-directed foraging; the result constrains the general principle, not the specific implementation.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Drosophila embryos deprived of proprioceptive feedback fail to develop functional locomotor central pattern generators. A pioneer premotor circuit of two segmental interneuron pairs autonomously generates rhythmic plateau potentials that drive muscle contraction; the resulting proprioceptive feedback is required for the gap-junctional coupling that builds the mature CPG.
mapping.ree_translation: A competence bootstrap can be entirely demonstrator-free, but it is not free of EXPERIENCE: an innate seed circuit generates its own activity, that activity generates its own training signal, and the mature competence is built from that closed loop. For CDQ-007 this is the mechanistic form the H-approach-primitive leg would need to take -- not 'an innate policy', but 'an innate activity generator whose output supplies the experience that trains the policy'.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The training signal is proprioceptive reafference in an invertebrate embryo, not reward or prediction error in a foraging agent. The general principle (self-generated activity bootstraps its own supervision) transfers; the specific signal, the gap-junction physiology and the IP3/Ca2+ pacemaking do not. Also a strong caution: it shows the innate seed alone is insufficient.
mapping.source_context: Calcium imaging and electrophysiology of emerging motor activity in intact and proprioception-deprived Drosophila embryos.

confidence_components.notes: Causal and mechanistically explicit, which is rare for this question. Held back by invertebrate-embryo transfer and by the fact that the signal channel has no clean REE counterpart.
